description: The extended window functions over a six-row two-department sales table: NTILE, PERCENT_RANK, CUME_DIST, RATIO_TO_REPORT, FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE and NTH_VALUE. The frame defaults are the point of several of them - FIRST_VALUE with the default frame reports the partition's first row for every row, and Snowflake's default frame for LAST_VALUE and NTH_VALUE is the WHOLE partition (RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING), so every row sees the partition's last value. Ties share a CUME_DIST, an out-of-range NTH_VALUE is NULL on every row, NTH_VALUE(x, 1) is FIRST_VALUE, and the RATIO_TO_REPORT values sum to 1. Converted 1:1 from functions/WindowFunctionsExtTest (now retired); the Java read individual row indexes out of a ResultSet with a 0.001 tolerance, which the suite replaces with whole-column LISTAGG renders at a fixed ROUND scale - every row is pinned rather than the two or three the Java sampled. The class's setupTest built the sales table, which each converted test recreates.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
SELECT id, NTILE(2) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS bucket FROM sales ORDER BY id
SELECT LISTAGG(bucket, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY id) FROM (SELECT id, NTILE(2) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS bucket FROM sales)
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
SELECT id, NTILE(3) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS bucket FROM sales ORDER BY id
SELECT LISTAGG(bucket, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY id) FROM (SELECT id, NTILE(3) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS bucket FROM sales)
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
SELECT id, amount, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY amount) AS pr FROM sales ORDER BY amount
SELECT LISTAGG(ROUND(pr, 4), ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY amount, id) FROM (SELECT id, amount, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY amount) AS pr FROM sales)
CREATE TABLE one_row (v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO one_row VALUES (42)
SELECT PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY v) FROM one_row
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
SELECT id, CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS cd FROM sales ORDER BY id
SELECT LISTAGG(ROUND(cd, 4), ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY id) FROM (SELECT id, CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS cd FROM sales)
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
SELECT LISTAGG(ROUND(cd, 4), ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY amount, id) FROM (SELECT id, amount, CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY amount) AS cd FROM sales)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cd) FROM (SELECT amount, CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY amount) AS cd FROM sales) WHERE amount = 150
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
SELECT id, RATIO_TO_REPORT(amount) OVER () AS ratio FROM sales ORDER BY id
SELECT LISTAGG(ROUND(ratio, 6), ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY id) FROM (SELECT id, RATIO_TO_REPORT(amount) OVER () AS ratio FROM sales)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(ratio), 6) FROM (SELECT RATIO_TO_REPORT(amount) OVER () AS ratio FROM sales)
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
SELECT id, FIRST_VALUE(amount) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS fv FROM sales ORDER BY id
SELECT LISTAGG(fv, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY id) FROM (SELECT id, FIRST_VALUE(amount) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS fv FROM sales)
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
SELECT id, LAST_VALUE(amount) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS lv FROM sales ORDER BY id
SELECT LISTAGG(lv, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY id) FROM (SELECT id, LAST_VALUE(amount) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS lv FROM sales)
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
SELECT id, NTH_VALUE(amount, 2) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS nv FROM sales ORDER BY id
SELECT LISTAGG(nv, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY id) FROM (SELECT id, NTH_VALUE(amount, 2) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS nv FROM sales)
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
SELECT id, NTH_VALUE(amount, 99) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS nv FROM sales ORDER BY id
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id, NTH_VALUE(amount, 99) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS nv FROM sales) WHERE nv IS NULL
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, amount DOUBLE)
SELECT COUNT_IF(a = b) FROM (SELECT NTH_VALUE(amount, 1) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS a, FIRST_VALUE(amount) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS b FROM sales)
